knowledge_refs.formula_empty_justification: The atom's nuclear structure is inferred qualitatively from rare large-angle alpha-particle scattering; no major reusable formula is applied.

hints: A deflection through more than 90° requires a strong interaction with a concentrated region of the atom.
Recall the charge of an alpha particle and the charge needed to repel it strongly.
Use the rarity of these large deflections to infer where most of the atom's mass is located.
walkthrough: An alpha particle scattered through more than 90° has experienced a very strong repulsive interaction.
Because an alpha particle is positively charged, the repelling nucleus is charged.
Only a very small, concentrated region can cause these rare large deflections, so the mass is concentrated in the very small nucleus.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the nucleus is charged.
States that the mass is concentrated in a very small nucleus.

knowledge_refs.formula_empty_justification: The charge of a named quark flavour is recalled as a particle property; no major reusable formula is applied.

hints: Recall the two charge groups for quark flavours: up-type and down-type.
The strange quark is a down-type quark.
walkthrough: Quarks of flavours down, strange and bottom each have charge −1/3 e.
The strange quark therefore has charge −1/3 e.

ai_rubric.observable: States the strange-quark charge as −1/3 e.

knowledge_refs.formula_empty_justification: The charge balance identifies a valid quark flavour from recalled particle charges; no major reusable formula is applied.

hints: Let q be the charge of each of the two identical-charge quarks, then add all three quark charges to give +e.
Use the strange-quark charge from part (i), then identify quark flavours with the resulting charge.
walkthrough: The strange quark has charge −e/3, and each of the other two quarks has charge q.
Their total charge is +e, so 2q − e/3 = e.
An up quark has charge +2e/3, so both remaining quarks may be up quarks. Charm or top quarks are also possible because they have the same charge.

ai_rubric.observable: Forms 2q − e/3 = e and deduces q = +2e/3.
Identifies up as a possible flavour for both quarks; charm or top are also accepted.
